result.note: Tests the August 2026 India–Japan maritime framework, the July 2026 first co-development agreement (UNICORN) and the MQ-9B lease.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–Japan maritime defence framework signed in August 2026:
items: It was signed by the two defence ministers, Rajnath Singh and Shinjiro Koizumi.
It covers maritime-domain awareness, information sharing and closer naval operations.
It grants the two navies immediate reciprocal access to each other's ports and repair facilities.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the two sides will only work towards reciprocal access to ports and repair facilities. The navies will also expand exercises, ship visits, logistics and coordination protecting sea routes.
questions.source: On Thursday, defence ministers Rajnath Singh and Shinjiro Koizumi signed a framework covering maritime-domain awareness, information sharing, and closer naval operations.

questions.prompt: At their July 2026 summit, India and Japan signed their first defence co-development agreement. Which system did it cover?
questions.explain: The July 2026 summit produced the first defence co-development agreement, for the Unified Complex Radio Antenna system, with a commitment to explore more projects. In August 2026 the defence ministers sought further cooperation in mine countermeasures, unmanned systems and naval shipbuilding.
questions.source: The statement follows July’s summit, where the two countries signed their first defence co-development agreement for the Unified Complex Radio Antenna system

questions.prompt: In August 2026, India leased two drones to provide persistent surveillance over the Indian Ocean. Which drones were these?
questions.explain: India leased two MQ-9B Sea Guardian drones in the same week that it signed the maritime framework with Japan. Together they reflect a model that combines national surveillance hardware with information from chosen partners.
questions.source: This week, India leased two MQ-9B Sea Guardian drones to provide persistent surveillance over the Indian Ocean
